keyAndScale.primaryKey: D major (C major shapes relative to Capo 2)

scalesUsed.notes: C - D - E - F - G - A - B - C
scalesUsed.application: Provides the melodic intervals (parallel 3rds and 6ths) that form the signature intro and verse riff
Shapes the conversational, evocative vocal phrasing delivered by Tracy Chapman

keyAndScale.modalCharacter: Ionian (Major) with introspective, bittersweet folk-pop intimacy
keyAndScale.keySignature: 2 sharps (F#, C#) sounding / Natural (no sharps/flats) relative to Capo
keyAndScale.relativeMinor: B minor sounding (A minor relative to capo)

mainProgression.description: The hypnotic four-chord progression in C shapes (sounding D major with Capo 2). Starting on the subdominant Cmaj7 gives the groove an immediate floating, unresolved sensation that mirrors the narrative desire to escape.

sectionProgressions.description: The iconic two-measure fingerpicking riff moving from open Cmaj7 and G up the neck to high-register Em and D dyad voicings
Full, passionate open-chord acoustic strumming elevating the emotional peak of the song
Gradual dynamic crescendo bridging the intimate fingerpicked verse into the soaring chorus
Diatonic third intervals along the 5th and 2nd strings outlining the sliding fingerpicking voicings

harmonicFunction: Cmaj7 (IV) - Subdominant chord establishing the wistful, yearning harmonic foundation
G (I) - Tonic chord offering brief grounded comfort before continuing the journey
Em (vi) - Relative minor introducing melancholy reflection and tension
D (V) - Dominant chord propelling the progression smoothly back to the IV chord

techniques.name: Two-Finger Hybrid / Fingerstyle Plucking
techniques.description: Simultaneously plucking the bass root with the thumb while plucking upper melodic strings with index and middle fingers, punctuated by quick hammer-ons

notes: Thumb plays bass notes on strings 5 and 6
Index and middle fingers pluck strings 2 and 3
Hammer-on: open B string hammers to 1st fret (C note) immediately following the initial pinch
Keep notes crisp with a light percussive snap against the fretboard
sequence: Pinch 5th string (3rd fret) and 2nd string (open) simultaneously
Hammer index finger onto the 1st fret of string 2
Pluck open G string (string 3), then brush the 2nd string
Pinch 6th string (3rd fret) and 2nd string (open) for the G chord
Slide up to fret 7 on string 5 and fret 8 on string 2 for the high Em voicing
Drop two frets down to fret 5 on string 5 and fret 7 on string 2 for the D voicing
tips: Do not lift your hand too far off the strings during the position shift to fret 7
Keep your thumb planted slightly ahead of your fingers for rock-solid timing
Lock into the 104 BPM groove without rushing the high-register slide

techniques.name: Dynamic Strumming Transition
techniques.description: Seamlessly transitioning from delicate, intimate fingerpicking in the verses to full, resonant acoustic strumming in the chorus

notes: Tuck your pick into your palm (or use bare thumb/fingers) during the verse
Open up into broad down-up strums on full cowboy chord shapes for the chorus
Control right-hand dynamics so the volume jump feels natural and powerful
sequence: Maintain quiet, steady fingerpicking through the narrative verses
Crescendo slightly on the pre-chorus lines
Strum full, ringing chords across all 6 strings when hitting 'So remember when we were driving'
Decrescendo smoothly back to the fingerpicked riff as the verse returns
tips: If playing with a pick, use hybrid picking (pick on bass, fingers on treble)
If playing bare-fingered, use the back of your fingernails to strum the chorus for clarity
The emotional impact of Fast Car depends on this dynamic contrast

sections.name: Intro Riff
sections.description: The instantly recognizable acoustic motif. Tracy Chapman pinches the Cmaj7 and G chords, then glides up the fretboard to the 7th and 8th frets.
notes: Capo on 2nd fret of your acoustic guitar
Simultaneous pinch of the bass note and treble note on beat 1
Snap hammer-on to the 1st fret of the B string
Clean slide up to frets 7 and 8 for the soaring Em color
sections.exerciseLabel: Tracy Chapman Iconic Fingerstyle Acoustic Riff

sections.name: Verse
sections.description: The intimate storytelling verse repeats the signature fingerpicked riff under the quiet, hypnotic vocal narrative.
notes: Keep right-hand velocity steady and understated
Let the open strings breathe behind the vocal lines
Lock into the 104 BPM tempo with a relaxed metronome pulse

sections.name: Chorus
sections.description: The song opens up dramatically into full, ringing open-chord strumming as the narrator remembers driving fast and feeling alive.
notes: Explode into full acoustic strumming across all six strings
Accent downstrokes on beats 2 and 4
Hold the D chord at the end of the phrase before returning to the intimate riff

sections.name: Scale Practice Exercise
sections.description: Two-string dyad scale study outlining the sliding 3rd and 6th intervals across strings 5 and 2.
notes: Pluck strings 5 and 2 together while muting string 3 and 4 with the flesh of your fingers
Slide smoothly between positions without lifting off the fretboard
Listen to how the sliding shape defines the entire song's harmony

guitar.recommended: Small-Body or Grand Concert Acoustic Guitar (Guild D-40, Martin 000-18)
alternatives: Any 6-string acoustic guitar with clean fret access up to fret 8
guitar.pickup: Under-saddle transducer or stereo acoustic condenser mics

amp.recommended: Acoustic combo amplifier or direct studio preamp
alternatives: Direct box into modern PA system

effects.other: Kyser or Shubb quick-change acoustic capo placed on the 2nd fret

beginner.title: Learn the Chorus Strumming First
steps: Clamp your capo on the 2nd fret
Practice open C, G, Em, and D chord shapes
Master the chorus progression (C - G - Em - D) with simple downstroke strumming at 90 BPM
Sing the chorus melody along with your strumming

intermediate.title: Master the Fingerpicked Intro Riff Mechanics
steps: Break down Measure 1: the Cmaj7 pinch and immediate hammer-on to 1st fret B string
Practice the shift to the G chord pinch with accurate thumb placement
Practice the neck shift up to frets 7 and 8 on strings 5 and 2
Loop the two-measure riff slowly with a metronome at 75 BPM before speeding up to 104 BPM

advanced.title: Seamless Transitions & Full Solo Performance
steps: Master switching effortlessly between fingerpicking the verse and strumming the chorus
Add subtle body percussion (hitting the guitar top with your thumb) on beats 2 and 4
Perform the full 5-minute song maintaining rock-solid tempo and storytelling emotion
Sing with dynamic control from whisper-quiet verses to belted choruses

commonMistakes: Missing the hammer-on timing — the hammer to the 1st fret happens immediately after the pinch
Looking down and hesitating when sliding up to the 7th/8th fret position
Accidentally muting the open G string during the high-register slide
Playing the chorus at a different tempo than the verse
practiceRoutine: 2 minutes: Capo check and checking fret 7-8 intonation
5 minutes: Isolated looping of the Cmaj7 pinch and hammer-on at 80 BPM
5 minutes: Position shift drill: jumping from open G to frets 7/8 and resolving to frets 5/7
5 minutes: Practicing the transition into the full-strum chorus
5 minutes: Full run-through playing along with the original track
focusAreas: Accurate finger placement on the high neck dyads
Dynamic control between verse fingerstyle and chorus strumming
metronomeWork: Start at 75 BPM looping the two-bar intro riff until it flows without hesitation
Gradually increase tempo by 3-5 BPM until you reach 104 BPM
Practice playing with the metronome on beats 2 and 4 to develop natural acoustic swing
Record yourself to verify smooth volume transitions between sections
